subject: MAP: Benchmark evidence delivery & exec readout scheduling
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Katie Johnson <katiej@bluewave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: MAP deliverables: Performance test plan + evidence to close by Aug 28

Hi all,

Per our MAP (timeline attached), BlueWave has asked for a structured performance evidence bundle to unblock procurement and an exec-level readout ahead of their internal steering committee. I sketched out the minimum deliverables we should include in the MAP milestone for "Performance Validation":

- Test plan (protocol + configuration) that reproduces BlueWave's production prompt mix and concurrency profile (see config attached: benchmark-test-config.json)
- Raw CSV exports with per-request timings (TTFT, token counts, tokens/sec) and aggregated P50/P95/P99 latency buckets
- Dashboard links (Grafana) with canned views for latency, throughput, and cache hit rates
- Slide deck (2–4 slides) summarizing results, callouts, and recommended model/quantization/scale for launch
- Executive one-pager + a short (15min) readout slot in the MAP close week

Target close on the purchase order: Aug 28. Proposed MAP milestone for evidence delivery: Aug 18 — internal dry run; Aug 20 — delivery to BlueWave; Aug 24 — exec readout prep; Aug 26 — exec readout with BlueWave steering committee. The MAP spreadsheet (MAP_BW-4721_v3.xlsx) I attached maps these dates to owners.

Questions for the team:
- Marissa / Karthik: can you validate the test harness config will exercise concurrency lanes up to 64 concurrent sessions and a 3:1 short-prompt to long-prompt distribution?
- Marissa: can you produce the CSV exports and the Grafana read-only dashboard link?
- Laura / Sergio: do you agree to run the exec readout with Katie/Tom on Aug 26 (15 minutes)?

Katie — is that timeline workable on your side? Any hard date constraints we should know about?

Thanks,
Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Katie Johnson <katiej@bluewave.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@bluewave.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP deliverables: Performance test plan + evidence to close by Aug 28

Thanks Aditya — that looks sensible. A couple of narrow asks from my side before you execute tests: 

- Please be very explicit about the TTFT definition you use. For our ops report we define TTFT as the time from request ingestion to emission of the first non-empty token at the socket. P50/P95 using that measurement is what our infra team looks at.
- We need concurrency scenarios for both steady-state (30 concurrent) and burst (64 concurrent) with a simulated user think-time profile — can you include both in the CSVs and label them clearly?
- Exec readout — we want Redwood to focus on risk areas (cold KV cache, tokenization overhead on our longest prompts) and recommended guardrails. If possible, send slides at least 48 hours before the readout.

Aug 26 exec time window is fine but we prefer morning PST (8:30–10am).

Looking forward to the artifacts.

Best,
Katie

Katie Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering — BlueWave Analytics
katiej@bluewave.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Katie Johnson <katiej@bluewave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP deliverables: Performance test plan + evidence to close by Aug 28

Thanks — quick methodology note and links to the working artifacts. I've run a smoke pass against a representative snapshot of BW prompts. High-level:

- Test harness: containerized runner using replay profiles derived from BlueWave samples. The config (benchmark-test-config.json) includes: concurrency lanes [30, 64], prompt distribution (short:long = 3:1), kv-cache-warmup policy (10 warmup requests per key), and tokenization seed lists.
- Metrics captured: TTFT (as Katie defined), per-token throughput (tokens/sec), request-level latency (P50/P95/P99), and aggregate throughput (reqs/sec and tokens/sec). We also capture CPU/GPU utilization and GPU mem utilization.
- Artifacts available: Grafana dashboard (read-only link below), CSV export for each run (filenames include run-id + concurrency label), slide draft summarizing: objectives, environment, key numbers (P50/P95 TTFT, tokens/sec, steady-state concurrency charts), and recommended capacity profile.

Working links / artifacts:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/bench/BW-4721-dashboard
- CSVs (S3): s3://redwood-evidence/BW-4721/benchmark-results.csv (contains multiple runs; split by run_id)
- Slide draft (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-ExecReadoutSlides

Attached to this email for internal review: benchmark-results-BW-4721.csv (filtered exports), and a short README in the benchmark folder that describes column headers. I'll also attach a condensed CSV labeled with concurrency in the filename for easy ingestion into BlueWave's perf team.

Preliminary highlights (from smoke runs):
- Steady-state (30 concurrent): P50 TTFT ~ 110ms, P95 TTFT ~ 260ms, aggregate throughput ~ 2.4k tokens/sec
- Burst (64 concurrent): P50 TTFT ~ 140ms, P95 TTFT ~ 420ms, tokens/sec scales near-linearly until KV cache drop-offs where we see tail increases

Caveats: the longest prompts (>= 1024 tokens) show a higher P95 due to tokenization and KV cache misses; we'll call that out explicitly in the executive slides with mitigations (pre-tokenization, optimistic KV warming).

Next steps:
- I'll export a per-run CSV with clear run labels and upload to the S3 path by EOD Aug 15.
- Aditya / Laura: I'll hand the slide deck to you both for narrative polish by Aug 18.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
